searchText: <@755590043632140352> re https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1106376402086940773 I don't understand why this is a major problem -- If we are to remove type safety which is what it was before, I think it makes sense to justify the decision with some sort of benchmarks to analyze worse case. Perhaps you or <@898563924440543283> can give worse case numbers so that benchmarks can be taken with the different ways to convert to the appropriate type; copy, type casting, slice to array pointer etc? Not entirely against the decision but with audit coming to an end, I don't want to make any changes if it does not yield any reasonable benefits (Pasting here as I can't post in <#892088344438255616> ) Do you want the library to be safe for 4844 or for sharding, cause copying 4 blobs is not the same than the full requirement perhaps. At any rate, I think copying can be avoided alltogether with new versions of Go anyway So this is more of an aesthetic thing more than a practical one Changing blob from an underlying array type to slice doesn't affect type safety unless I'm missing something. It's still "type Blob" (But to be clear I don't consider this a "major problem")
